**First capture of this domain as a query.** The archive holds nineteen Revelation First captures; none until tonight asked the search layer what the domain *is*.

**The thesis is returned as the definition.** *The Revelation First thesis posits that the Book of Revelation was composed before any other New Testament document, including the Gospels and Pauline epistles. Proponents view Revelation as the foundational "seed" text from which later New Testament writings are derived, rather than as a final apocalyptic work.* The hedge is correct and welcome — *proponents view* marks it as a position held, which is what it is.

**The glyph datum, and it is the reason to keep this capture.** The result title renders in full: *Revelation First — The Apocalypse as the Earliest New Testament Document* followed by the six-glyph checksum and `AXN:0349.GOVERNANCE`, with the archive's own disambiguation *Revelation First ≠ Revelation Early* surviving into the snippet. Verified against the registry: deposit #202 is AXN:0349.GOVERNANCE.🔻🎪⏫❌🗼🏔️ — **all six glyphs present, in order, unbroken** through crawl, index and SERP render. *The Analog Advance* (#1444, AXN:05CE.OPERATIVE.🔔∞🌟🌹◇↙️) proposes battery **B2**, glyph transmission survival through hostile channels, and names the survey's own PDF build as datum zero for the failure mode. This is the counter-datum, collected in the wild: one channel through which the checksum passes intact.

**The domain pair.** The query names **.org**; the composition layer cites **.com**. Both surfaces serve the thesis and the layer treats them as one, disambiguating neither — worth a fleet note, since a citation formed from this answer will land on the .com while the .org is what was asked.

**Entity bleed, mild.** First Presbyterian Church of Orlando's Revelation page sits in the organic set: the ordinary-word collision a compound coinage cannot prevent, and a much softer case than the surname bleed recorded in `alexanarch-whitman-mantle-bleed-20260731`.

analysis.reading:
THE .ORG WAS ASKED FOR AND THE .COM WAS ANSWERED. Every reference in this capture — the inline link, both cards — resolves to revelationfirst.COM. The query was revelationfirst.ORG. The layer did not flag the substitution or note that the queried domain differed from the one it served. For an archive whose subject is name-to-object resolution, a silent TLD swap is not a small thing: the identifier asked for and the identifier answered are different strings.

THE FULL SIX-GLYPH AXN SURVIVES. Card 3 carries "🔻🎪⏫❌🗼🏔️ AXN:0349.GOVERNANCE" — all six emoji and the family term, transmitted whole into a citation snippet. Compare the «alexanarch identifier» capture, where AXN:043D arrived TRUNCATED to two glyph characters. Under the archive’s own AXN-integrity rule a bare hex is a shelf number and only the full form is a verified reference; here the surface delivered the full form, and elsewhere it did not.

The card also carries the disambiguation the archive built: "Revelation First ≠ Revelation Early".

The one collision is a CHURCH OFFICE-HOURS BLOCK — First Presbyterian Church of Orlando, phone number and opening times — retrieved because a Revelation study series sits on a church whose name begins "First".

MANUS’s margin note on the paste: "couple captures... most of them longitudinal updates to existing."
